strengths: Strong theoretical contributions with rigorous formalization: Theorem 1 establishes exponential separation (TIME(2^O(S(n))) vs TIME(O(S(n)))), while Theorems 3-5 provide clean separation results and optimality guarantees for recursive vs non-recursive approaches
Elegant formalization bridging classical recursion theory with modern Transformers through complexity-theoretic analysis, with two independent proofs of main result increasing confidence

Convincing experimental results on SAT: 3B model achieves 98% (easy) and 95% (medium) accuracy vs 88% and 64.8% on much larger frontier models; Figure 3 compellingly shows active context stays bounded while trajectory length grows exponentially
Comprehensive treatment with multiple variants, extensions to heterogeneous models and tool-use, detailed appendices with proofs and implementation guidance
Novel perspective establishing recursion depth as fundamental computational resource, proving problem decomposability (shown necessary) is also sufficient for exponential power gains
weaknesses: Severe theory-practice gap: Theory assumes O(log S(n))-precision arithmetic (unavailable in practice), hardcoding of TM transitions (unclear generalization), and 2^O(S(n)) recursion depth (experiments show much shallower trees). No analysis of learnability from finite data.

Extremely limited experimental scope: Only SAT evaluated—arguably the easiest case for recursion with obvious backtracking structure. No cross-domain validation, single model size (3B), weak baselines from other papers without controlled comparison, and no ablations or architecture studies.

Incomplete treatment of critical practical challenges: Error accumulation inadequately addressed (1 paragraph for exponentially deep recursion); trace generation strategy (DPLL) not shown to generalize; KV cache management, infinite recursion handling, and training efficiency not discussed.

Weak connection between theorem proof and actual learning: Theorems construct algorithms (STATE, POS, CELL, etc.) that model must somehow learn from examples, but no analysis of training data requirements, generalization to larger inputs, or robustness to arithmetic errors in learned approximations.

Experimental design issues: Baseline results from different papers without direct comparison; Figure 3 incomplete (doesn't show context variation with problem structure); no error bars or significance testing; only 2-20 variables shown despite claims about scaling.

strengths: Rigorous theoretical framework establishing exponential separation between deep recursion (TIME(2^O(S(n)))) and single-context approaches (SPACE(S(n))), with formally correct proofs via two independent methods
Novel local/global space decomposition providing elegant perspective on context management with practical implications for GPU/external memory offloading
Theorems 4-5 establishing optimality of recursive models within broader class of agentic systems is a strong theoretical contribution
Clear experimental demonstration on SAT: 3B model outperforms frontier LLMs (GPT-4o, Qwen3-235B) with superior context efficiency (Figure 3)
Well-grounded connection between classical recursion theory and modern Transformer-based reasoning through constant-depth Transformer realizability with O(log S(n)) precision
Clear presentation with effective illustrations (Figure 1) and comprehensive appendices with detailed proofs and implementations
Honest discussion of limitations including error accumulation, inference efficiency, and practical considerations
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: idealized Transformers assume arbitrary O(log S(n)) precision and ability to learn canonical configuration embeddings (Embed function), but real models use finite precision and may not learn these structured behaviors

Experimental validation limited to single task (SAT with natural recursive structure); lacks evaluation on other long-horizon reasoning domains (planning, theorem proving, code generation) and comparison to alternative context management methods (summarization, memory augmentation)
Double-exponential step complexity (2^2^Θ(S(n))) without memoization remains expensive even with memoization (2^O(S(n))); practical cost-benefit analysis missing

Practical applicability unclear: paper assumes recursive decomposition exists but provides no algorithm for designing decompositions for arbitrary problems; sensitivity to decomposition quality unexplored
Use of average-hard attention (AHA) in proofs differs from practical softmax; impact of finite-temperature approximations not analyzed
Limited error analysis: 64% accuracy on hard instances but systematic failure modes not investigated; error accumulation mitigation (discarding intermediate reasoning) not empirically validated
Experimental scope narrow: only 3B parameter model tested with limited ablation studies (recursion depth impact, decomposition strategy sensitivity, training efficiency not reported)

Training requirement for ground-truth recursive reasoning traces may be impractical for new domains; related work on concurrent recursive proposals (Sun et al. 2025, Zhang et al. 2025a) weakens novelty of core observation despite theoretical novelty
